about: Human verdicts read (never written) by scripts/media-pixel-guard.mjs. /media is served immutable for a year, so a file under public/ that is modified between two revisions must show identical decoded pixels and animation timing (images, after EXIF orientation) or identical copied packets, stream parameters, side data (display matrix), packet timing and first decoded frame (videos); PDFs and other types must be byte-identical. Any other change fails the guard unless this list holds an entry for that exact path and that exact pair of blobs: {"path": "public/media/<name>", "baseBlob": "<full blob id at the base revision>", "headBlob": "<full blob id at the head revision>", "verdict": "approved" or "rejected", "who": "<the person who compared both>", "when": "YYYY-MM-DD", "note": "<optional: what changed and why it may ship>"}. The guard prints both blob ids on every failing line. A verdict covers only that pair: any later change to the file needs a new entry. The aegean-bone law (SKILL.md section 2) allows no exception to 'never publish different pixels under an existing /media name' other than a proven metadata-only rewrite, so an approval here is the owner's exception to that law, and browsers that cached the old bytes keep showing them for up to a year.
